name: Rails 7+ Patterns
description: Enforces Rails 7+ conventions including Hotwire, Turbo, Stimulus, and modern Rails architecture.
content:
# Rails 7+ Patterns Rules

- Use Hotwire (Turbo + Stimulus) for interactivity — avoid adding React/Vue/Angular unless you have a specific SPA requirement
- Use Turbo Frames to update parts of the page — wrap dynamic sections in `<turbo-frame>` tags
- Use Turbo Streams for real-time updates — `turbo_stream.append`, `turbo_stream.replace` for server-pushed changes
- Use Stimulus controllers for JavaScript behavior — small, focused controllers that connect to DOM elements
- Use `has_many :through` over `has_and_belongs_to_many` — join models give you a place for extra attributes and validations
- Use Active Record scopes for common queries — `scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }` instead of class methods
- Use `strict_loading` to prevent N+1 queries — enable globally in development to catch missing eager loads
- Use Action Cable for WebSocket features — integrate with Turbo Streams for real-time broadcasting
- Use Active Job with Solid Queue (Rails 8) or Sidekiq for background processing — never do slow work in request cycle
- Use `credentials.yml.enc` for secrets — never store secrets in `ENV` without Rails credentials as the primary source
- Use database-level constraints (`null: false`, `index: { unique: true }`) — don't rely solely on model validations
- Use importmap-rails for JavaScript dependencies — avoid Node.js/Webpack/esbuild unless you need a build step
